main_conditions: Stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma
Lung cancer with mediastinal nodal involvement
other_conditions: Mother with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer
expanded_sentences: The patient is a 53-year-old female diagnosed with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, specifically adenocarcinoma, originating in the right upper lobe of the lung.
She presents with severe chronic cough and exertional dyspnea, symptoms that have progressively worsened over the past year.
Her medical history includes a significant smoking history of approximately 15 pack-years, although she quit smoking 7 years prior to her cancer diagnosis.
Recent laboratory tests have shown mild elevations in hepatic transaminase levels, which are being monitored during her systemic therapy.
A CT-guided biopsy confirmed the presence of lung adenocarcinoma, and subsequent genetic testing revealed an actionable EGFR exon 19 deletion.
She is currently undergoing treatment with osimertinib, an oral medication, at a dose of 80 milligrams.
A CT scan of the chest was performed, and her baseline carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level was measured at 42.7 ng/mL prior to initiating first-line systemic therapy.
There is a family history of breast cancer, as her mother was diagnosed with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in her early sixties.
